non_blocking_required_findings.body: Closure at the head the approval will actually bind. The template defines readiness_head as the head that contains the committed final review, i.e. a child H** of 01d8565a, not 01d8565a itself. The evidence in declaration v3 is anchored at ancestors: the narrowed CI gate is observed only at d690a967 (field named observed_at_8456f206_lineage, no run recorded at 8456f206 or 01d8565a), validate-contract/machine-preflight are recorded as 'at d690a967 and later', and the byte-identical executor rebuild is at 8456f206. The v3 ci_gate.rule says 'exact-head CI at the readiness head', so as written the rule is again not demonstrated at the bound head. The executor will fail safe on any bound-file drift (validate_static rehashes the code manifest and every authority binding; repository_preflight requires HEAD == origin == authority.git_head, clean), so this is a recording gap, not a known-failed precondition as in cycle 02.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: Template readiness_head 'the ... head that contains the final review; must equal origin at authorize time'; declaration v3 ci_gate.rule vs ci_gate.observed_at_8456f206_lineage.head d690a967; admission_contract.m1_ultra_checks_at_d690a967_and_later; executor.rebuild_at_readiness_head_8456f206; operator_procedure_assertions[0].
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: Before authorize, bank an append-only readiness note for H** recording: (a) git diff --stat 01d8565a..H** showing only the banked review evidence files added and nothing under crates/, Cargo.lock, specs/017-rust-native-inference-runtime/, scripts/research/, docs/validation/, docs/research/glm52/raw/, with declaration v3 (269babfb...), contract v3 (7f984043...) and binding (c582e3b4...) shas unchanged; (b) the exact-head CI outcome for H**: classification and Apple Silicon workspace baseline results, or, if the docs-only classification skips the baseline, that fact plus the empty crates diff back to d690a967; if the FULL_NATIVE job runs, confirm the MLX small-fixture failure is still only at generate_f017_v11_measurement_v1.py --check; (c) validate-contract PASS and machine-preflight PASS executed on the M1 Ultra at H** with the pinned environment. No code change; no new cycle.

non_blocking_required_findings.body: Two stale sha256 references inside the sha-bound corrected-oracle binding (c582e3b4..., itself verified by validate_static and reachable from the approval through contract v3). The binding pins the checkpoint-free reconciliation at f7193decd52081942a50c267754ce614699638c6773c0e818e3e22bf483d484e, while declaration v3 and the inlined file (same path) carry 7af5cd9da4d8625c8a890d4a67ad913d5166f0218c41ca80f06b34f4d2ac2c34; the binding pins the inert template at 07fc9d55976f6d8dc32f547cb0049ba99403beb81c8a7348095f0f5a80d1475c, while the inlined template hashes to bb70347dd6d44ab1483da08d58bdc968e6f109a946452886058bb40b7e4cb5b2. Cause visible in the commit list: in-place edits after the binding was pinned at 5e32d68f (30ca81dc 'evidence wording updated' matches the reconciliation's changed synthetic_differential wording; 01d8565a 'inert template rebound to v3'). This contradicts the 'evidence banked append-only' claim and repeats the in-place-mutation pattern behind cycle-02 B-02, but validate_static checks neither nested field, neither file participates in execution, and the documents the human directly binds (declaration v3 -> reconciliation 7af5cd9d; contract v3 -> binding c582e3b4) are mutually consistent, so the GO can be made informed without re-binding.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: CORRECTED-ORACLE BINDING checkpoint_free_reconciliation.sha256 and template.sha256 vs DOMAIN DECLARATION v3 checkpoint_free_reconciliation.sha256 and the inline template header sha; contract.rs validate_static generation-3 block checks only attempt_id, expected_token, acceptance_mode, live_authorization_created, primary/secondary_selected_token; COMMITS 30ca81dc and 01d8565a.
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: Record both stale references, their cause and their non-effect on execution in the same append-only readiness note and in the human approval body; do not issue a binding v2 now (it would force contract v4 and another cycle for no execution benefit); from here on, no in-place edit of any file that a sha-bound document references, including the template (create template-v2 if it must change again).

non_blocking_required_findings.body: Minted-authority inspection. execute-evidenced-v4 cross-checks attempt_id, contract sha, executor sha, manifest/catalog/checkpoint-set shas and the D0/D1/D2/D3.5/synthetic/ledger values, but it does not assert authority.expected_token == contract.one_shot.expected_token (154820) or authority.prompt_token == 9703; agreement rests on f017_native_p1_authorization.py (sha-bound in the manifest but not inlined) and on validate_real_p1_authority (not inlined). The classification at p1_domain.rs 1304-1311 and the math constructed at bounded_p1.rs use authority.expected_token, so the authority file is the single point that decides what counts as success.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: bounded_p1.rs execute-evidenced-v4 arm authority binding block (no expected_token/prompt_token comparison); FullNativeP1MathV3::new(..., authority.expected_token); math.execute_one(&context, authority.prompt_token); addendum R-02 'by construction'.
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: After authorize and before execute, the operator reads the minted authority JSON in the fresh state root and records in the readiness note: attempt_id == F017-NATIVE-BOUNDED-P1-ATTEMPT-2, expected_token == 154820, prompt_token == 9703, contract_sha256 == 7f98404333b0661f42c0e44f0a6c6451282513531a978dd442a98dafbfe94af8, executor_sha256 == 91e50a0bb84a30450f9189da2122b84e1790649c1361ed90cea001ca537f52f0, checkpoint_set_sha256 == d7d1e6a8f8ab11726a7f1e43e4d8f02ed73f04ee27ffb876915147a568b9afee, git_head == H** == origin; abort before invoking execute-evidenced-v4 on any mismatch (nothing is spent before durable start).

defense_in_depth_findings.body: The executor has no explicit runtime assertion that the authority's one-shot tuple equals the contract's one-shot tuple (expected_token, prompt_token, attempts, retries, resume, mandatory_stop); today the guarantee is by construction of the authorization script.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: bounded_p1.rs authority binding checks; validate_static enforces the contract side only.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: For a future contract generation (not now, no code change for attempt 2), add the tuple equality to the execute-evidenced arm and a negative control for it; R-03 covers attempt 2 manually.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: FullNativeP1MathV3 is constructed with authority.expected_token. The token should be inert to the forward pass and argmax and used only for evidence labelling; the packet does not show this.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: By inspection, record every use of the expected_token field inside executor.rs with file:line and confirm none reaches the math or the produced-token path; also enumerate stream::EXPECTED_TOKEN uses in executor.rs, which the R-02 disposition did not cover.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Shard rehash placement and duration. SHARD_IDENTITY_REHASH reads ~222 GB; attempt 1 took 123.5 s and the M1 Ultra cannot page-cache 238 GB, so a hash pass followed by the forward pass may exceed the stated 2-3 minutes, and it is unstated whether the rehash happens before or after the durable-start consumption point (a hash-time failure after durable start spends the attempt).
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: declaration one_shot.shard_identity, expected_duration, consumption_rule; contract shards total ~238 GB.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Record whether the rehash precedes durable start; run under caffeinate; do not interpret a run longer than 3 minutes as a hang; bank actual phase timings in the execution-evidence record.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: The 'gate-path only' characterization of wrapper change 5b39a21a (+53/-9 in f017_corrected_oracle_primary_wrapper_v11.py) is asserted, not shown; Event 06 (154820) ran with it while the V11 measurement pins the pre-change wrapper. The graph module and decoders are byte-identical and cross-checked by N1/N3, so this only bears on the oracle's context construction (prompt 9703, position 0, empty KV, mask).
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Tell the human, in the approval body, that a native result other than 154820 does not by itself discriminate a native defect from an oracle-context defect; the discriminator is the evidenced-v4 payload (79-layer fingerprints, full logits) compared against the Event 06 payload hashes pinned in the binding.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Declaration v3 cites p1_domain.rs ~1090 as the execution comparison; the inlined snippet there is the legacy RECEIPT_SCHEMA path (mismatch returns Err), while the evidenced-v4 classification is the 1304-1311 block. Both use authority.expected_token, so the conclusion stands, but the citation is imprecise.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Correct the citation in the readiness note; no code change.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Nothing in the executor prevents a second authorize creating a fresh state root and a new authority after a terminal failure; the no-retry rule is a governance control only, and the approval is committed only after the run.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Immediately after the run, bank the receipt/terminal record and commit the approval before any other action on the machine; treat any further authorize under approval 2 as prohibited by record, not by tooling.

rationale: Cycle-02 B-01 and B-02 are closed on their merits: declaration v3 is a new append-only file that replaces the failed CI precondition with an explicit narrowed gate and records the V11 drift, its cause (5b39a21a vs f35d3411), its ancestry to the Event 06 source and its independence from the executor; the packet inlines declaration v3, contract v3, the binding, the template and the reconciliation verbatim with full sha256s, and the template carries the v3 declaration sha and the full contract sha. R-01..R-03 are satisfied with substance: the only numerical delta since attempt 1 is the IQ4_XS lane-order fix (four tensors) with an honest open prior, the durable-start rule and post-failure scope are in the bound declaration; the verdict and stop logic use authority.expected_token in both the legacy and the evidenced-v4 paths and stream::EXPECTED_TOKEN is test-only; the oracle numerics and decoder modules are byte-identical at c3526d68 and the readiness head. D-01..D-05 are closed (byte-identical rebuild, quit-not-suspend, shard rehash, reviewer provenance). The generation-3 validator is closed-schema, keeps generation 2 frozen, sha-binds the corrected-oracle document and checks its token, mode and both selected tokens against a compiled constant; all seven negative controls reject; the execute-evidenced-v4 arm binds executor identity, contract sha, repository head/origin/cleanliness, machine, dylibs, environment and memory, and the legacy arms are tombstoned. The corrected token 154820 is well supported (primary binary64 and secondary f32 agree, 3.53 top-1 margin, pinned payload hashes, public evidence commit). Residual issues found are governance-recording gaps, not execution defects: the bound head will be a child of 01d8565a and the gate evidence is at ancestors (R-01); the sha-bound binding carries two stale pointers to informational documents that were edited in place after pinning (R-02), which I judged non-blocking because validate_static does not consume them, they cannot affect what executes, and the documents the human directly binds are mutually consistent; and the executor relies on the authorization script rather than an explicit assertion for the expected-token/prompt-token agreement (R-03). With R-01..R-03 recorded before authorize, the domain is fit for one human GO for exactly one bounded M1 Ultra native P1 under execute-evidenced-v4, mandatory stop, no retry, no resume. The human's prior GO was not treated as evidence.
